extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and attorneys before the USPTO; OED staff; disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and sanctions applied by the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline for professional misconduct by registered patent attorneys/agents, including specific regulatory provisions proscribing dishonesty, mishandling client funds, failure to withdraw when incapacitated, and related procedural requirements for suspension and reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) – dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied here to taking unearned legal fees and USPTO fees paid by a client and converting them for the practitioner's benefit and by misrepresenting to the client that the work had been performed while submitting eight fictitious trademark application numbers as representative of the client's application numbers. Example facts: Respondent received advanced fees and costs totaling $7,605, did not perform work, misrepresented fictitious application numbers, and converted funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) – other conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes engaging in other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to characterize misconduct beyond explicit dishonesty—here coupled with §10.23(b)(4) to reflect that conversion of funds and misrepresentations adversely reflect on fitness to practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.40(b)(3) – withdrawal when mental/physical condition impairs performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires a practitioner to withdraw from employment when the practitioner's mental or physical condition renders it unreasonably difficult for the practitioner to carry out the employment effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violation found where practitioner continued representation during a period in which physical conditions made it unreasonably difficult to carry out duties (e.g., serious medical condition and caregiving responsibilities). The rule is a standard for when continued representation is improper and withdrawal is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a) – failing to seek lawful objectives / failing to carry out contract / intentionally prejudicing client
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes intentionally failing to seek the lawful objectives of a client through reasonably available means, intentionally failing to carry out a contract of employment entered into with a client for professional services, and intentionally prejudicing or damaging a client during the course of a professional relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where practitioner failed to perform agreed work (filing eight trademark applications), collected legal and USPTO fees for unperformed work, and did not promptly return fees and costs not used. This provision governs substantive failure to perform contracted professional obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.112(a) – deposit client funds in identifiable accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires a practitioner to deposit funds of clients paid to a practitioner or a practitioner's firm, except advances for costs or expenses, into identifiable bank accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violation found for failing to deposit $2,600 in advanced costs for USPTO filing fees into a trust or identifiable account. This rule controls handling and segregation of client funds and identifies when funds must be placed in a trust/account.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.112(c)(4) – promptly pay or deliver client funds on request
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires a practitioner to promptly pay or deliver to the client as requested by a client the funds, securities, or other properties in the possession of the practitioner that the client is entitled to receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where client requested refunds (March 2013) of filing fees and legal fees and the practitioner did not promptly refund any part until March 3, 2014. This criterion defines the obligation to return unearned fees and unused costs without delay upon client request.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1) – discipline in another jurisdiction as a USPTO rule violation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes being disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by any duly constituted authority of a State (i.e., state discipline can constitute a violation of USPTO Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here, the practitioner's suspension by the Supreme Court of California (Feb 23, 2015) is identified as a violation under USPTO Rules and is an independent basis for discipline before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreed sanctions and conditions of suspension (Final Order provisions a–j)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order imposes specific sanctions and administrative conditions: suspension from practice for four (4) months; remain suspended until OED Director grants petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60; comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon request for reinstatement; dissociate practitioner's name from Customer Numbers and PKI certificate; prohibition on applying for/obtaining a USPTO Customer Number or having name added to one until reinstated; electronic publication of the Final Order in OED's FOIA Reading Room; publication of a notice materially consistent with the Official Gazette Notice of Suspension; Office may consider the record in future proceedings; each party bears its own costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order sets both punitive and administrative requirements for reinstatement and public notice. The Official Gazette notice text summarizes the violations and mitigating considerations (remorse, restitution, medical/family circumstances). The conditions reference other regulatory provisions (e.g., 11.58, 11.60) practitioners must follow when seeking reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to make restitution and interest where unearned fees were converted
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must return unearned attorney fees and unused USPTO filing fees and may be required to pay interest on refunded amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter Respondent refunded $7,605 (unearned fees and costs) and later paid $1,154.88 as interest. The Order treats restitution and interest payment as relevant remedial actions and mitigating evidence but does not substitute for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors considered in discipline (medical, family, remorse, counseling, no prior OED history)
rubrics_metrics.description: When deciding discipline, the OED Director may consider mitigating circumstances such as serious medical conditions, substantial family responsibilities, remediation efforts (psychological counseling, Lawyers Assistance Program attendance), remorse, full restitution, and absence of prior OED disciplinary history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Suspension explicitly lists these considerations (e.g., respondent's serious medical condition beginning Aug 2011, caregiving duties, prompt counseling and remediation steps, restitution and interest payment, and no prior OED disciplinary history over 19 years) as factors weighed in reaching the settlement and sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notification requirements for disciplinary orders
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided Notice of Suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication includes specific content summarizing violations, sanction, and mitigating factors; the Order also requires dissociation of Customer Numbers and PKI and warns that the Office may consider the record in future proceedings. Publication is both public notice and part of disciplinary remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural jurisdiction and statutory bases for USPTO disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director has jurisdiction pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies the statutory and regulatory authorities under which disciplinary proceedings, settlements, and Final Orders are issued by the USPTO and OED.
